subject: Physics
question: A 1500 kg car accelerates along a straight road. Calculate its kinetic energy (a) when its speed is 12 m s⁻¹ and (b) when its speed is 20 m s⁻¹, and (c) the work done by the resultant force between these two moments.
response_text:
(a) $v = 12\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: $E_k = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1500 \cdot 12^2 = 1.08 \times 10^{5}\ \text{J}$

(b) $v = 20\ \text{m s}^{-1}$: $E_k = \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1500 \cdot 20^2 = 3.0 \times 10^{5}\ \text{J}$

(c) By the work–energy principle, $W = \Delta E_k = 3.0 \times 10^{5} - 1.08 \times 10^{5} = 1.92 \times 10^{5}\ \text{J} \approx 1.9 \times 10^{5}\ \text{J}$.

The resultant force does about 190 kJ of work, which is the gain in the car's kinetic energy.
